subject: Civil Engineering
title: Dynamic Compaction: Dropping Heavy Weights
description: One-minute skill: Dynamic Compaction: Dropping Heavy Weights.

hook.text: Drop a 20-ton weight from 60 feet and it compacts loose soil on impact.

buildup.text: Repeated drops create craters that are backfilled. The ground densifies with each hit.

discovery.text: Ménard developed the technique in France — it treats large areas fast and cheaply.

twist.text: Vibrations travel far — nearby buildings need monitoring during every drop.

climax.text: Airports, ports, and reclamation sites use dynamic compaction for millions of square feet.

punchline.text: Sometimes the best engineering is dropping something heavy.

quiz.question: What is a major limitation of dynamic compaction?
options: It only works on rocky terrain
Vibrations from impacts can damage nearby buildings
It requires extremely specialized equipment not available worldwide

details.summary: Dynamic compaction densifies loose granular soil by repeatedly dropping heavy weights of 10 to 40 tonnes from heights of 10 to 40 meters using a crane. The impact energy compacts the soil to depths of 3 to 12 meters.
details.whyItMatters: Dynamic compaction is one of the most economical ground improvement methods for large areas of loose fill or natural granular deposits, commonly used on reclaimed land and industrial sites.
takeaways: Weights of 10 to 40 tonnes are dropped from 10 to 40 meters repeatedly
Effective improvement depth reaches 3 to 12 meters depending on energy input
It is most effective in loose granular soils and fills above the water table

faq.question: What determines the effective depth of improvement from dynamic compaction?
faq.answer: The depth of improvement is proportional to the square root of the product of drop weight and drop height. Heavier weights dropped from greater heights improve deeper soil. Empirical formulas estimate depth as roughly 0.5 times the square root of weight times height in metric units.

faq.question: What are the limitations and environmental impacts of dynamic compaction?
faq.answer: Ground vibrations limit use near existing structures and sensitive utilities. Noise levels are very high. It is ineffective in saturated fine-grained soils where pore pressure cannot dissipate between impacts. Crater impacts can temporarily liquefy saturated sand.
